youtube_title: The 1918 circus train wreck near Hammond, and Showmen's Rest
body: 4 in the morning. A troop train's engineer fell asleep. On June 22, 1918, a Hagenbeck-Wallace circus train had stopped on the tracks between Hammond and Gary, and an empty troop train slammed into it from behind. About 86 people died, and more than 100 were hurt. Five days later, dozens of them were buried together outside Chicago, at Showmen's Rest. Most of the graves are marked Unknown. Stone elephants stand around the graves, trunks lowered. Visitors say they've heard elephants trumpeting there. The nearby zoo hasn't had elephants since 2010.
